feature: Add Mobile Navigation Menu to Landing Page
workflow_rationale: This is a single-file, frontend-only UI enhancement with no backend dependencies. It adds a hamburger menu for mobile users to access navigation links that are currently hidden on mobile viewports.

phases.name: Mobile Navigation Implementation
phases.description: Add hamburger menu and mobile navigation overlay to the landing page Navigation component

subtasks.description: Convert Navigation to client component and add hamburger menu icons

changes: Add 'use client' directive at the top of the file
Create MenuIcon component (hamburger icon with 3 horizontal lines)
Create XIcon component (close X icon) following the CloseIcon pattern in modal.tsx

icon_specs.MenuIcon: Three horizontal lines (≡) using SVG rect or line elements
icon_specs.XIcon: Two diagonal lines forming an X, similar to CloseIcon in modal.tsx

verification.expected: File contains 'use client' directive and both icon components

subtasks.notes: Successfully converted page.tsx to client component by adding 'use client' directive at the top. Added MenuIcon and XIcon components inline following the pattern from modal.tsx. Removed metadata export as it's incompatible with client components (metadata should be in layout.tsx). Verification passed: 'use client' directive and both icon components are present in app/page.tsx.

subtasks.description: Add mobile menu state management and hamburger button

changes: Add useState hook for isMobileMenuOpen state in Navigation component
Replace the mobile 'Başla' button (lines 372-378) with a flex container containing both hamburger button and 'Başla' button
Hamburger button should be visible only on mobile (md:hidden)
Add onClick handler to toggle isMobileMenuOpen state

ui_requirements.button_style: Simple icon button with padding, hover effect, and transition
ui_requirements.layout: Flex row with gap between hamburger and 'Başla' button

verification.expected: File contains useState for mobile menu state

subtasks.notes: Successfully added mobile menu state management with useState hook in HomePage component. Created hamburger button in Navigation component that toggles between MenuIcon and XIcon based on isMobileMenuOpen state. Button includes proper accessibility attributes (aria-label, aria-expanded) and keyboard support. Verification passed: useState for mobile menu state is present in app/page.tsx.

subtasks.description: Create mobile menu overlay with navigation links

changes: Add mobile menu overlay that appears when isMobileMenuOpen is true
Create backdrop overlay with semi-transparent background
Create slide-in menu panel from the right or top
Add close button (X icon) at the top of the menu
Include all navigation links: Özellikler, Fiyatlandırma, Giriş Yap
Include primary CTA button: Ücretsiz Dene
Add onClick handlers to close menu when a link is clicked
Add transitions for smooth open/close animation

ui_requirements.backdrop: Semi-transparent dark overlay that closes menu when clicked
ui_requirements.z_index: Higher than navigation (z-50 for nav, use z-[60] for mobile menu)
ui_requirements.close_behavior: Close on backdrop click, close button click, or link click

accessibility.keyboard: Escape key should close menu (optional but recommended)
accessibility.aria_labels: Add aria-label to hamburger and close buttons

checks: Hamburger menu button visible on mobile viewport (< 768px width)
Clicking hamburger opens mobile menu overlay
Mobile menu contains all navigation links (Özellikler, Fiyatlandırma, Giriş Yap, Ücretsiz Dene)
Clicking a link closes the menu
Clicking X button closes the menu

subtasks.notes: Mobile menu overlay successfully implemented with all required features: backdrop click to close, X button, escape key handler, all navigation links (Özellikler, Fiyatlandırma, Giriş Yap, Ücretsiz Dene), smooth slide-in animation, body scroll lock, and mobile-only visibility (md:hidden). Follows the modal.tsx pattern.

parallelism.speedup_estimate: Sequential implementation required (subtasks build on each other)

acceptance_criteria: Mobile users can access all navigation links via hamburger menu
Menu closes properly on all interaction types
No console errors or TypeScript errors
Page builds successfully with npm run build
